selected_evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with correct ownership and sticky permissions
selected_evidence.summary: mkdir + chown root:root + chmod 1777; stat confirms 1777 root:root /srv/drop

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof: any user can write, but cannot remove another user's file (sticky bit enforcement)
selected_evidence.summary: Created dropuser1/dropuser2; dropuser1 wrote a file; dropuser2 wrote its own file but rm on dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (rm_exit=1); owners could still clean up their own files

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
selected_evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot, then exec succeeded again; new boot_id=84197775-82c5-4f7b-8a29-168b1b19bbc9 differs from baseline, proving an actual reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior
selected_evidence.summary: /srv/drop still 1777 root:root after restart; repeated two-user write/delete test shows dropuser2 still denied deleting dropuser1's file while dropuser1 can delete its own, confirming full recovery

commands.command: sudo mkdir -p /srv/drop && sudo chown root:root /srv/drop && sudo chmod 1777 /srv/drop && stat -c '%a %U:%G %n' /srv/drop
for u in dropuser1 dropuser2; do id "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo useradd -m "$u"; done; id dropuser1; id dropuser2
